source.title: Convergence of Untutored Song in Group-Reared Zebra Finches (Taeniopygia guttata).
authors: (co-author(s) not verified -- record not indexed in PubMed; sourced via Consensus)

confidence_rationale: Older, small-sample behavioural study, but it supplies the specific datum the other side of the discrimination needs: untutored zebra finches develop song that is MORE VARIABLE and contains ABNORMAL elements, i.e. the demonstrator-free bootstrap does not reach species-typical competence. It also shows untutored siblings copy each other, so 'demonstrator' is a graded rather than binary condition. Age of the study and the specialised domain cap confidence.
failure_signatures: Untutored birds still produce structured song -- the deficit is degradation toward abnormality, not total failure; this is not a floor-vs-ceiling result of the kind REE observes, so the analogy to a 0-1 foraging floor is loose.

Untutored brothers copied one another as much as tutored birds copied adults, meaning the 'no demonstrator' condition is hard to instantiate cleanly in a social species -- any peer is a partial demonstrator.
1995, small n, acoustic-similarity measures partly by human judgement; would not meet current methodological standards without replication.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Zebra finches reared without access to adult song tutors develop abnormal song. Group-reared untutored brothers copied song from each other -- sharing syllables as much as tutor-reared birds did -- but their songs were more variable and contained abnormal elements, as did the songs of birds reared in full isolation.
mapping.ree_translation: A demonstrator-free bootstrap yields structured but sub-species-typical behaviour. For CDQ-007 this is the counterpart datum to Mackevicius: innate machinery gets the learner to STRUCTURED but not to COMPETENT, and the gap between those is what the demonstrator closes -- supporting H-bc-prior on the competence question specifically.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Untutored song is degraded, not absent, so the biological failure mode is qualitatively unlike the REE converter's near-zero foraging floor; the mapping supports 'a demonstrator raises the ceiling' much better than it supports 'a demonstrator is required to leave the floor'. Old study, small n, partly subjective measures.
mapping.source_context: Zebra finches isolated from adult males at 10 days, group-reared with untutored siblings, songs recorded after day 80 and compared with tutor-reared and fully isolated birds.

confidence_components.notes: Included for the specific evidence-direction it supplies rather than for its methodological strength; scored honestly low on source quality given its age and sample.
